Hey all.. I'm one of the crowd who's looking into migrating from Windoze to Linux (currently working with Debian Mint/LMDE). One of the things I do Daily is control my HTPC from my laptop. This means turning it on with a WoL magic packet (haven't gotten this far yet) and remote mouse/keyboard.

In my current environment (all Win7), I've been using Win2VNC for years and am quite happy with it. I have 3 different computers that can all connect to and control my HTPC. The same person also have X2VNC, which would be ideal as I'm only looking to move one computer to linux for the time being. But unfortunately I can't get it to work and have NO clue how to troubleshoot.... if someone else might, I connect without issue but the mouse is never picked up by my HTPC screen.

I know about synergy and am trying to get it configured, but I'm not sure it's designed for my type of use (multiple servers, one client), instead being featured for the exact opposite (one server, many clients). Plus, I'd love to be able to use my android tablet as the remote (mouse) and there is no android server with synergy. Doesn't help that I see a lot of complaints out there in regards to the direction that synergy is headed.

So, other multi-platform options? I'd just as soon continue to use VNC, but certainly don't know enough to write my own much less troubleshoot something someone else wrote nearly a decade ago.
Help sorting out one of my "daily essential" needs

xvnc4viewer

apt-get install xvnc4viewer

WoL Magic Packet with linux

apt-get install etherwake

Then, you just type in a terminal (you can always bind it to a key-combo):

etherwake MAC-ADDRESS-OF-HTPC-HERE

xvnc4viewer does the Exact opposite of what I want. It brings the video (only) to my laptop, and leaves me with no control of the HTPC at all. I don't want/need video, only mouse/keyboard input.

But I did setup WOL and created a .sh file to automate the process (while I remember the IP, the MAC is a different story... lol), thanks there... I just hadn't bothered to look before getting input control functional.

You may also want to look into avahi-daemon for name resolution over your LAN. With avahi you can connect to other machines on your network by using domainname.local instead of having to remember IP addresses for every machine on your network.
